Case_09009/figure11.jpg.source_caption: Lactophenol cotton blue stain of culture growth.

description.short_caption: Lactophenol cotton blue stain showing fungal hyphae and spore structures.
description.detailed_description: This image shows a lactophenol cotton blue stain of fungal culture growth. The stain highlights branching septate hyphae and round spore-like structures, which are characteristic of certain fungal species. The blue coloration is due to the stain binding to fungal cell walls, providing contrast against the background. The structures are well-defined and typical of fungal morphology under light microscopy.

description.short_caption: Chest radiograph showing bilateral pulmonary infiltrates.
description.detailed_description: This is a frontal chest radiograph displaying the thoracic cavity. There are bilateral pulmonary infiltrates, more pronounced in the right lung, with areas of increased opacity suggestive of consolidation or infection. The cardiac silhouette appears normal in size, and the bony structures, including the ribs and clavicles, are intact. No obvious pleural effusion or pneumothorax is visible.
visible_findings: increased opacity in the right lung

description.short_caption: Axial CT scan of the chest showing bilateral lung abnormalities.
description.detailed_description: This axial CT image of the chest demonstrates bilateral lung fields with areas of abnormal opacification. The right lung shows a large region of consolidation with air bronchograms, suggestive of infection or inflammation. The left lung appears to have smaller, patchy opacities. The mediastinum and heart are centrally located, and no significant pleural effusion is visible. The scan is presented in a soft tissue window.
visible_findings: right lung consolidation with air bronchograms
patchy opacities in the left lung

description.short_caption: H&E stain at 40x magnification showing fungal elements and necrotic tissue.
description.detailed_description: This histopathology image, stained with hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) at 40x magnification, shows pink-stained necrotic tissue with scattered dark brown to black fungal elements. The fungal structures appear as irregularly shaped, branching hyphae. The background is composed of amorphous necrotic debris, and there is no clear evidence of intact cellular architecture.
visible_findings: dark brown to black fungal elements

description.short_caption: Coronal CT scan of the chest showing bilateral pulmonary abnormalities.
description.detailed_description: This coronal CT scan of the chest reveals bilateral pulmonary findings. There are areas of patchy opacities in both lungs, suggestive of possible consolidation or infiltrates. The mediastinum appears central, and no obvious pleural effusion is visible. The scan is de-identified and does not include contrast enhancement.

description.short_caption: CT-guided drainage of a pelvic abscess.
description.detailed_description: This axial CT image of the pelvis shows a hypodense fluid collection consistent with an abscess. A percutaneous drainage catheter is visible, positioned within the collection. Surrounding soft tissue structures are visible, with no obvious bony destruction. The image demonstrates the use of CT guidance for abscess drainage.
visible_findings: hypodense fluid collection in the pelvis

description.short_caption: Cytology of aspirate showing branching filamentous structures.
description.detailed_description: This image shows a stained cytology specimen from an aspirate. The field contains branching, filamentous structures that are stained pink to red, consistent with a modified acid-fast or Gram stain. The background is relatively clear, with minimal cellular debris. The morphology suggests filamentous bacteria, possibly Actinomyces or Nocardia species.

Case_09009/figure7.jpg.source_caption: Wet prep, with calcofluor white stain, under fluorescent microscope.

description.short_caption: Calcofluor white stain under fluorescent microscopy showing fungal hyphae.
description.detailed_description: This image shows a fluorescent microscopy view of a calcofluor white-stained sample. The bright green fluorescence highlights branching fungal hyphae, which are filamentous structures characteristic of certain fungi. The background is dark, enhancing the contrast of the fluorescent structures. The stain binds to chitin and cellulose in fungal cell walls, making it a specific tool for identifying fungal elements.

description.short_caption: GMS stain of lung tissue showing fungal elements, 40x magnification.
description.detailed_description: This is a photomicrograph of lung tissue stained with Gomori methenamine silver (GMS) at 40x magnification. The image highlights branching fungal hyphae, which appear black against a green background of tissue. The hyphae are septate and show acute-angle branching, consistent with a fungal infection. The GMS stain is commonly used to identify fungal organisms in histopathological samples.

description.short_caption: H&E stain at 10x magnification showing tissue necrosis and inflammatory infiltrates.
description.detailed_description: This histopathology image, stained with hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) at 10x magnification, shows areas of tissue necrosis characterized by eosinophilic debris and loss of normal architecture. Surrounding the necrotic regions, there is evidence of inflammatory infiltrates, including dense clusters of cells consistent with neutrophils. The upper portion of the image appears more cellular, while the lower portion shows more extensive necrosis.
